observations: Predicted $35 given 10/5 clicks, values X7 Y6 Z1 and a harm-based payment.
Honest bid7 gave top slot, payment35 and profit35: other bidders' value fell from65 to30.
Bid3 gave second slot, payment5 and profit30; bid10 tied honest profit35; bid0 gave no slot/payment/profit.
The visual shows the externality gap and profit at each integer bid. Reveal explicitly refers back to honest7 even while the current control remained at0.

complexity.reason: Arithmetic is simple but distinguishing bid, value, payment and profit needs attention.

whyCool: Trying to game the price visibly shows why truthful bidding can be optimal.
caveat: The observed fixed opponents support this example; the general dominant-strategy claim requires the mechanism's broader argument, not just this one utility curve.
effort: Completed prediction, four bid states, visual inspection and reveal.
bucketReason: Rich controlled comparisons and a clear externality visualization.

prediction.reason: Explicit values permit calculating the externality rather than guessing an unknown pricing convention.

interaction.reason: Bid comparisons and a losing boundary expose allocation, payment and utility separately.
interaction.evidence: Tested bids0,3,7,10 and the plotted integer utility profile.

payoff.reason: Correctly connects original prediction, observed harm and incentive to report value.
payoff.evidence: Honest7 and inflated10 both profit35 versus low3 profit30.

clarity.reason: Current bid and historical honest-bid explanation are clearly distinguished.
clarity.evidence: Reveal says At the honest $7 while current bid remains0.

transfer.reason: A pricing principle is stated without a different valuation case.

surprise.reason: Paying less can leave less profit; inflating a bid does not improve this allocation.
surprise.evidence: Bid3 pays5 but keeps30 versus honest keeps35.

visualExplanation.reason: Externality bars and full utility profile explain price and incentives together.
visualExplanation.evidence: Without/with X bars plus integer bid profits.

playfulness.reason: Bid manipulation is the core experiment.

depth.reason: Links externalities, allocation and incentive compatibility.
depth.evidence: Payment determined by others' lost value.
